items.source_expression: Elapsed time and review-count mass are nonnegative in the fixed and responsive models.
items.lean_expression: The complete elaborated atoms expose the same additions, products, powers, divisions, expectations, inequalities, and finite normalizations shown by the source formula.
items.source_domain: Prior shape and strength, Bernoulli quality, elapsed review count, finite product sets, and conditional probability laws are interpreted on their cited source-model domains.
items.lean_domain: Lean uses real-valued model scalars, natural finite indices where exposed, finite carriers, and PMF expectations for the corresponding source quantities.
items.source_operations: The source uses addition, subtraction, multiplication, squaring, division, finite averaging, expectation, square root, maxima, and strict or weak inequalities as appropriate to this item.
items.lean_operations: The elaborated Lean atoms use the same real operations, finite sums or PMF expectations, square root, maximum, and strictness direction after paper definitions are expanded.
items.source_coercions: Rating and selection counts enter real-valued ratios and posterior formulas through the ordinary natural-to-real embedding; qualities and prior parameters remain real-valued.
items.lean_coercions: Lean embeds natural counts and finite cardinalities into the reals before division and otherwise retains the source real-valued arithmetic domain.
items.source_division: Every model denominator is interpreted on the source's valid Beta, positive-time, nonempty-set, or positive-lifespan domain; the unfairness divisor convention is stated explicitly in the interface.
items.lean_division: Lean uses real division with the same displayed denominator; theorem rows expose source-domain positivity where needed, while formula definitions are total extensions outside that model domain.
items.source_rounding: None of these reviewed formulas performs floor, ceiling, integer truncation, or numerical approximation in its mathematical statement.
items.lean_rounding: The reviewed Lean atoms perform no floor, ceiling, integer truncation, or approximate arithmetic operation.
items.source_normalization: MSE and unfairness normalize by finite market or quality-class size, selection rate normalizes by lifespan, and probability expectations use unit-mass laws.
items.lean_normalization: The same finite-cardinality, lifespan, and unit-mass PMF normalizations are visible in the expanded definitions and conclusions.
items.source_strictness: The source uses weak monotonicity for squared bias, printed strict variance monotonicity with the corrected interior domain, and weak convexity or concavity inequalities.
items.lean_strictness: Lean preserves each weak or strict comparison, and separately proves weak closed-interval variance decrease, strict interior decrease, and both strict endpoint failures.
items.source_zero_denominator: The source model supplies valid priors, positive elapsed counts where required, nonempty maxima, and meaningful lifespans; empty quality classes are outside the empirical conditional statistic.
items.lean_zero_denominator: The theorem rows establish denominator positivity from their visible conditions; total formula rows explicitly choose zero for an empty quality class and otherwise agree on the source domain.
items.relation_basis: After the ordinary count-to-real embedding and the stated finite-standard-deviation convention, every exposed arithmetic operation and inequality direction is the source formula itself or a proved algebraically identical expansion.
